clue.text: Successfully confront, getting back up presumably

definitions.meaning: to face someone down is to stare or stand them out until they give way
someone lying prone has their back turned upwards

explanation.surface: A person beats an opponent and is getting their fighting spirit back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to outface an opponent and to lie prone, so one's back is uppermost.

clue.text: Note author's celebrity

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
the setter, as author, refers to himself as me; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: A short message mentions how famous some writer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity and renown are synonyms for being widely known.

clue.text: Love killing, but strangely calm in prison, see?

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are arranged in a strange, unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone jailed for a murder of jealousy seems oddly serene behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' scrambles CALM IN PRISON SEE into the French phrase for a crime of passion; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a murder committed out of sexual jealousy or passion, a killing for love.

clue.text: For openers, fixer is popularly believed dead

parts.note: a door is something for opening, here an entrance one opens

explanation.surface: A locksmith's first moves are thought to have killed something off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'dead as a doornail': the thing popular speech holds to be dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'dead as a doornail' makes this object the proverbial example of lifelessness.

clue.text: Bird? Get one right away from jailer

indicators.note: signals that the letter for right is taken out of the word for jailer

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks a prison guard to release a captive bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from WARDER leaves the bird; 'Get one' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A wader is a long-legged shore bird such as a heron or sandpiper.

clue.text: Cheap ticket admitting husband and youngster once

indicators.note: letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a saver is a discounted rail ticket in Britain

explanation.surface: A discount fare lets a married man and a child travel.
explanation.walkthrough: A SAVER is a British cut-price rail ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaver is a dated, jocular word for a boy or lad, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Care about short distance, being used to the area

indicators.note: around, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to heed is to take care or notice
ft, the abbreviation for foot or feet, is a short distance

explanation.surface: Someone takes care over a short walk while getting to know the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: A hefted flock of hill sheep knows its own stretch of open grazing and stays on it without fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Hill farmers call sheep hefted when they have learned and keep to their own patch of moorland.

clue.text: One making slow progress, going after source of tobacco plant

indicators.note: placed behind, so the creeping piece follows the tobacco piece

parts.note: Virginia, the US state, is famous for its tobacco

explanation.surface: Something slow-moving heads for where tobacco comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing vine with red autumn leaves is a familiar ornamental plant.

clue.text: College clubs were good at athletics

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
runners who were good ran well

explanation.surface: Students at a college were strong at track events.
explanation.walkthrough: CRANWELL is the RAF college in Lincolnshire, where Britain's air force officers train.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranwell is the Royal Air Force college, an officer-training establishment.

clue.text: Way to shop by sort of train that may be standing at Bank

parts.words: that may be standing at Bank
parts.note: a standing order is a regular payment set up at a bank

explanation.surface: A train stationary at Bank, the London Underground station, suggests a shopping method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the London Tube station where a train stands, but it is a bank where a standing order is set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering goods by post from a catalogue is a long-established way of shopping.

clue.text: Run into bad weather, taking old pass up

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a storm, crossing an ancient mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a mountain pass in the surface; with 'up' it is the definition, to go without.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to give it up or pass it up voluntarily.

clue.text: Anxious Widmerpool should admit point

indicators.note: letting in, so the point goes inside the name

parts.note: Kenneth Widmerpool is a character in Anthony Powell's novel sequence A Dance to the Music of Time, shortened to Ken
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A nervous fictional schemer ought to concede a point in debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious in the sense of eager to do something is a close synonym.

clue.text: Wall covering may be one translation

definitions.meaning: plaster or cement coating applied to an outside wall
a version of a text put into another language

explanation.surface: A coating on a wall might be one version of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a coat of plaster on a wall and a translation or interpretation.

clue.text: Official publication used by Gilbert's journal?

parts.note: Gilbert White was the 18th-century naturalist of Selborne
a paper is a newspaper or journal

explanation.surface: A government document appears in some Gilbert's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert White kept the famous natural-history journals of Selborne, Hampshire; 'used by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A government white paper is an official report setting out policy proposals.

clue.text: Lay in hedge, off the ground

indicators.note: gone off, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something rested in a hedgerow rather than on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LAY IN HEDGE. HEADINGLEY is the Test cricket ground in Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Headingley is a famous cricket and rugby stadium, a sports ground in Leeds.

clue.text: Late on this platform, cyclist is disheartened

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy: the dead lie on this stand. 'is disheartened' removes K, the middle of BIKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the stand on which a corpse or coffin rests before burial.

clue.text: Perish, if encountering this at sea?

definitions.text: Perish, if encountering this at sea?

indicators.note: confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors could die if they met this vessel on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges PERISH IF; the whole clue also describes a burning vessel sent against an enemy fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel loaded with combustibles and set alight to drift among enemy ships could well destroy them.

clue.text: Nonsense one has to silence

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone talking rubbish needs to be shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Such a turn welcomed by theatre manager

definitions.meaning: a turn of 360 degrees, coming back to the start
a sold-out balcony tier in a theatre pleases its manager

explanation.surface: A theatre boss is glad to book a variety act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' suggests a variety act on stage, but it is a rotation; the circle is a theatre's upper seating tier.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a complete rotation and also a sold-out upper tier of theatre seats.

clue.text: Complain as doctor probes head

indicators.note: pushes into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A patient grumbles while a physician examines their skull.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan is to lament or complain about something.

clue.text: Screw in some distance in correct place

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Fit a screw some way into the right spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' looks like a verb, but a ship's propeller is called a screw.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's screw is its propeller, the bladed shaft that drives it.

clue.text: Get to break without seeing head

indicators.note: losing the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone takes a rest break without seeing the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at or get to it.

clue.text: Regular occasion finished early

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A routine function ended before time.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and regular are synonyms for steady or uniform.

clue.text: Praise that man for speaking out

indicators.note: said aloud, so the word is given by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone praises a man who speaks his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Praise' is a noun: a song of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a song of praise, typically to God.

clue.text: Dick Whittington's assistant not working

indicators.note: working the letters over, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dick Whittington's helper is idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Whittington is a classic British Christmas pantomime; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Whittington is one of the traditional stories staged as British Christmas pantomimes, a type of panto.

clue.text: Chastise dwarf that's careless

parts.note: to slap someone is to chastise them
Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: Telling off one of Snow White's dwarfs proves thoughtless.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphappy means casual and careless, cheerfully slapdash.

clue.text: Paladin's men return to country

explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns OR into RO; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roland is the most famous of Charlemagne's twelve paladins, his knightly peers.

clue.text: One accompanies the vulnerable in Cape Horn storm

indicators.note: storm-tossed, so the letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: A guardian escorts the helpless through a gale off South America.
